findings.text: _section_by_id re-implements a capability the repository already owns: reckon/_store.py:2264 _find_by_id(lst, ident, id_field='id') has the identical contract (scan a list of dicts for one matching id, return (index, record) or None). The module already imports from reckon._store (OpError, SectionRecord, _section_contract_refusal), so the lookup could call the owner rather than duplicate it; it duplicates, it does not extend.

The links case at line 170, the effort_hours case at line 186 and the capability case at line 200 assert only that the parsed record carries the change and that audit-doc is clean; none asserts that every other section's authored bytes are unchanged, which the done_when requires for each of the five fields. Only the title case (line 150) and the body case (line 225) take the other-section byte snapshot, so a typed-field write that disturbed a neighbouring section's authored HTML would pass the gate.

Setting the body of a section whose authored span is whitespace-only is refused with an internal match error rather than applied. For such a section section_field_spans returns a body span that is a bare newline (probe against the head module: section s1 with a record element and no prose yields body preimage '\n', which occurs 7 times in the document), and _replace_authored_html requires the preimage to occur exactly once, so the write raises 'must match exactly once; found 7 occurrences'. The refusal is safe (nothing is written) but it is unreachable-looking for a caller setting prose on an empty section, and the plan's own §4 deliverable phrases body as replacing authored HTML between the record element and the next heading, a span that can be empty.
